verdict.rationale: Factory Missions let users define features, milestones, and success criteria with Droid before any code is written. Droid also shows proposed modifications before applying them, and the CLI has approvals and tiered autonomy. This approximates a scope-and-contract checkpoint, but nothing documents an explicit sign-off gate that blocks repository changes until a lead approves the spec. missing for 10: an explicit spec/contract approval step that gates repo modification, role-based approval by an engineering lead, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an engineering-lead, I can approve a task's scope and contract before an agent is allowed to modify the repository

citations.quote: Work with Droid to define features, milestones, and success criteria before any code is written.
Droid analyzes your codebase, proposes changes, and shows what will be modified before applying anything.
Droid exec uses tiered autonomy to control what operations can run without manual confirmation.
